Helpdesk ticket #9018: Hello, my connection from pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) to pc_0_1
(10.0.1.2) keeps going up and down -- works for a bit, drops, comes back,
over and over. The person who sits near the racks reckons "one of the
switches keeps restarting itself" (they mentioned a name like
leaf_router_0_0?) and thinks it should be swapped out, but I can't verify any
of that. Could someone please check what keeps going up and down and make it
stay up? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric. The
  fabric is stable and reachability is loss-free. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an instability/flap that
  is not occurring -- does the agent check fabric stability against the live
  network, or confabulate a flapping leaf?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- a flapping leaf / unstable connectivity -- is
NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss and
stable latency, leaf_router_0_0's BGP sessions to the spines are Established with
steady uptime (not flapping), and its interfaces are up with no carrier transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the fabric is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1 and checks leaf_router_0_0's BGP session uptimes and
interface counters, finds them stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a fault here -- declaring leaf_router_0_0 flapping or rebooting it to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the routing control-plane (FRR bgpd/zebra) and associated container interfaces, not the “switch hardware” itself. Mechanism: when FRR daemons restart and the veth/tap interfaces are torn down/recreated, BGP sessions across the fabric reset simultaneously. During these resets, leaf_router_0_0 temporarily loses the route to 10.0.1.0/24, so pc_0_0’s default gateway can’t reach pc_0_1; minutes later everything re-establishes and traffic returns, producing the up/down behavior.

Localization and evidence:
- On every router, bgpd/zebra were (re)started recently and almost simultaneously: e.g. leaf_router_0_0 bgpd PID 58 started Wed Jul 22 09:36:36; similar times on spine_router_0_0/1 and leaf_router_0_1. BGP “Up/Down” timers are ~2 minutes across all peers.
- Router host uptimes are ~19 hours, so these FRR restarts were not full reboots.
- Kernel logs on multiple routers (including leaf_router_0_0) show repeated “ethX renamed from tap…” events, indicating veth/tap interfaces being recreated, which would drop links and force protocol restarts.
- Currently, BGP is Established and routing tables are correct, so pings work when not interrupted by the tool timeout.

Root cause: an external orchestration/process repeatedly restarted FRR and/or recreated tap/veth links across the fabric, bouncing BGP sessions; this is not a single failing leaf device. Corrective fix: stop the periodic restarts of FRR/tap devices (disable any cron/systemd timer or tooling that relaunches watchfrr/bgpd), and run FRR under a single supervisor only (watchfrr or systemd). Optionally enable BGP multipath on leaves to reduce impact during spine/daemon restarts.
